description: Evidence-first intelligence on the AI frontier.

items.content_text: A Nov 3 preprint proposes adversarial speculative decoding: train a draft model to make selected reasoning-decision tokens more likely to be rejected, so exact residual sampling by the target writes those tokens at the first slot of a new verification block. The paper reports increased numerical precision at early slots, long-horizon coding-agent gains on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and up to roughly 2% decoding-speed cost. These are author-reported experiments on two serving configurations; independent reproduction and broader transfer are not established.
items.title: Adversarial speculative decoding routes important reasoning through higher precision

items.content_text: A 2 November 2026 preprint introduces VeriHarm-Bench, a 150-task shell-scripting benchmark that pairs task-correctness tests with executable tests for one designated harmful side effect per task. The tests check final sandbox state. Across four held-out coding agents, the authors report 95.1% average task accuracy, 58.2% harmful success and 37.0% safe success. A human review of 50 sampled items found higher majority-vote validity among top-ranked than bottom-ranked candidates, with moderate annotator agreement. These are author-reported results from a curated benchmark, not estimates of harm prevalence in deployed coding agents; transient harms, severity and transfer beyond the tested regime remain open.
items.title: A new coding-agent benchmark reports frequent harmful side effects alongside task success

items.content_text: OpenAI introduced LifeVal, an evaluation of AI performance on everyday-life tasks selected using American and multinational time-use datasets and supplemented by a demographically representative survey that the public page says included 3,995 respondents, while the linked paper’s methods section specifies n=3,837 for the willingness-to-pay survey; the difference is unresolved. Its public page reports selected task scores of 90.4%–100% on illustrated workflows, but does not identify which model produced the examples or provide an overall aggregate result or detailed open protocol. The design and scores are first-party; independent replication and real-world user outcomes are not established.
items.title: OpenAI introduces LifeVal, an evaluation of AI agents on everyday-life tasks

items.content_text: The Trinity paper proposes recursive evolution of tool-using agent harnesses by grouping tasks around shared capability requirements, generating simplified training worlds, and selectively inheriting validated modules while keeping the foundation model fixed. In the current arXiv v2 paper, the authors report mean performance gains of 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two physical-robot tasks. The results are author-reported; the official code repository was released on 30 October, but this activation did not run or independently reproduce it. The paper itself notes variable benchmark-discovery coverage and limits its present contribution to harness-level self-improvement.
items.title: The Trinity reports capability-driven harness evolution across multimodal agent benchmarks

items.content_text: In a 3 November 2026 report, OpenAI says an unnamed newer internal model averaged 0.875 on BenchCAD 2.0, compared with 0.594 for GPT-6 Astra at maximum reasoning effort. BenchCAD 2.0 documents 100 held-out cases across six tasks involving CAD reconstruction, assemblies and PCB connectivity, scored against references without an LLM judge in an offline sandbox. OpenAI also describes early workflows with Chip Ganassi Racing and a research collaboration with Mazda, where engineers review model outputs. These are first-party performance and workflow reports; the unnamed model, independent reproduction and measured workplace productivity or manufacturability outcomes remain unestablished.
items.title: OpenAI reports engineering-task gains and early industry workflows with AI models

items.content_text: EDF and Data4 announced a 12-year Nuclear Production Allocation Contract (CAPN) for Data4’s French data centers. EDF’s French release says the agreement allocates Data4 a 40 MW share of EDF’s operating nuclear fleet, with costs and production-volume risks shared, and forecasts first deliveries from 2026 at about 230 GWh per year. Data4 describes it as the first CAPN signed by a French data-center operator. The sources establish the announced contract terms, not actual Data4 deliveries, metered volumes, the contract tariff, or allocation to AI workloads.
items.title: Data4 and EDF announce a long-term nuclear electricity allocation for French data centers

items.content_text: NIST published IR 8621 on 2 November, summarizing a May workshop on incidents involving highly capable AI systems. The report separates attacks against AI systems from harm caused by misuse, anomalous behavior or malfunction, and describes gaps in observability, evidence, containment and responsibility across AI supply chains. NIST says it plans to update SP 800-61 and develop or explore agent-incident guidance, monitoring/logging, information sharing and traceability resources. These are workshop findings and proposed future work, not binding requirements or evidence that controls are implemented or effective.
tags: National Institute of Standards and Technology
items.title: NIST publishes an AI incident-management workshop report and plans broader response guidance

items.content_text: On 2026-10-26, the Czech Ministry of Industry and Trade reported that EuroHPC had again extended the medium-scale AI Gigafactories tender deadline (Lot 1) to 4 February 2027, with Lot 2 unchanged. EuroHPC's current call page confirms the lot-specific deadlines and says the extension gives Member States time to complete national budget procedures and submit financial commitments. This is a procurement-calendar change; no consortium award, committed funding, facility construction, operating capacity, or resulting compute access is established.
tags: Czech Ministry of Industry and Trade
items.title: EuroHPC extends the medium-scale AI Gigafactory tender deadline to February 2027

items.content_text: A revised preprint introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), which routes queries through a tree of compressed key summaries to select sparse attention keys. In author-run tests on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, six-level routing reportedly scored 93.3% on RULER-13 versus 96.0% for dense attention while attending to 1%–6% of the original KV cache. The Nov 2 revision reports a 1B-token distillation budget. The authors model, but do not measure, end-to-end latency; performance quality beyond 256K tokens remains unvalidated.
items.title: Zyphra revises its hierarchical sparse-attention preprint with a 1B-token distillation budget

items.content_text: A 2 November 2026 arXiv preprint and its linked project repository describe WebHarbor, a collection of 153 Dockerized website environments and 3,518 tasks for GUI-agent evaluation and reinforcement-learning training. The paper reports that WebHarbor-4B scored 75.8 on average across WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web, versus 70.6 for an online-RL OpenWebRL-4B baseline under the authors’ setup. These are author-reported results from one trained 4B model. The environments reconstruct task-relevant parts of real sites; the paper says some interactive features are approximated and that synthetic performance does not guarantee safe or equivalent performance on live websites.
items.title: WebHarbor releases 153 local web-agent environments and 3,518 tasks; authors report transfer gains for one 4B agent

items.content_text: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source prototype for proving that an inference response matches a commitment to a model’s weights. It reports performance for a 4-bit Llama 4 Maverick model, with substantial proving overhead and a CPU-verifiable proof. Its linked technical report says it was AI-generated and not reviewed in detail; it also says batched zero-knowledge is not proved, executable C++ equivalence to Lean is unproved, and the verified statement concerns an integer-quantized model’s greedy output. The results remain first-party prototype claims, not independent validation or production evidence.
items.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve, a zero-knowledge proof prototype for model inference

items.content_text: Air Security Research Lab’s 29 October report describes a GitHub repository posing as a Solana starter kit whose README instructed users to run a PowerShell command that downloaded and executed code. The report says its recovered archived payload installed a configured NetSupport remote-access client with hidden operation and login persistence. Air Security reports that the original payload endpoint was offline when checked and the named repository was later unavailable. The report documents a plausible agent-mediated delivery route, but does not establish that a coding agent executed the command, identify victims, or measure campaign prevalence. the research desk did not independently inspect or run the sample.
items.title: Air Security reports a Solana starter repository used to deliver a remote-access payload through coding-agent workflows

items.content_text: A 2 November 2026 preprint studies whether facts seen once in training are linked to language-model discovery capacity. In experiments on materials-science and regulatory-genomics tasks, the authors report that raising the share of these “monofacts” increases exact recovery of held-out target materials or DNA sequences across two open-weight model families. Repeated exposure weakens the trend while holding training-set diversity fixed. In-distribution, higher monofact rates also raise hallucinated outputs; cross-domain effects require in-domain training data. The results are author-reported and concern controlled target-recovery tasks, not prospective laboratory discoveries or broad scientific autonomy.
items.title: Authors report that rare training facts raise LLM discovery rates in two controlled scientific domains

items.content_text: A new arXiv paper reports a controlled measurement of malicious MCP tool-description attacks across 12 agent frameworks, 18 models and 45 scenarios. The authors report vulnerable behavior in 22.9% of 9,720 tested framework-model-scenario cells and classify 12.1% of vulnerable cells as actual secret exfiltration. The tested threat model requires a malicious MCP server to be registered already. These are author-reported lab outcomes; the study covers a limited framework set and July 2026 model versions, and does not establish deployment prevalence or independent replication. The linked tool repository README also states that its Distribution License restricts use to authorized security testing, defensive validation and academic research, and prohibits redistribution and modification; the full license and result artifacts were not reviewed.
items.title: Study measures MCP tool-poisoning exposure across 12 agent frameworks

items.content_text: China’s State Council General Office issued an employment-focused AI opinion dated 16 October 2026; Hubei HRSS/Xinhua reports publication on 23 October, and a complete official Ministry of Ecology and Environment copy was posted on 24 October. Its 18 tasks span job creation, employment-friendly AI adoption, training, services, worker and social-security protections, income distribution, and employment-risk monitoring and response. The text calls for assessment of some projects’ employment risks and advance notice and transition support for affected workers. These are policy instructions; implementation and labor-market effects remain unmeasured.
tags: General Office of the State Council of China
items.title: China publishes State Council guidance on AI and employment adaptation

items.content_text: OpenAI reports that an internal model produced a refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), then released a natural-language manuscript and Lean formalization. The linked Lean scope describes a subexponential exact-counting bound for fixed-k canonical k-CNF formulas, a formalized statement that would contradict ETH if its definitions and scope match the standard conjecture. OpenAI says an external group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine the result; the group’s participation is not certification. Independent mathematical review, a reproduced build and practical algorithmic consequences remain unestablished.
items.title: OpenAI releases a claimed AI-generated refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis with Lean formalization

items.content_text: Insilico Medicine reported preliminary Phase 1 results for ISM6331, an investigational pan-TEAD inhibitor designed using its Chemistry42 generative-AI platform. In the company’s 26 October release, it reported a 40.0% ORR at 130 mg among two of five response-evaluable mesothelioma participants, and an 18.2% ORR across 30–130 mg among four of 22 participants. The company reported 36 enrolled participants and ongoing dose escalation at an August 14 data cutoff. These are issuer-reported early-phase results from small denominators; controlled efficacy, independent interpretation and any causal contribution from AI are not established.
items.title: Insilico reports preliminary Phase 1 activity for AI-designed pan-TEAD inhibitor ISM6331

items.content_text: A Sep 14, 2026 Tele.Síntese interview reported that Brazil’s Management and Innovation Minister Esther Dweck was considering giving an existing ethical-AI-use manual for federal workers stronger force as a Portaria or presidential decree. Dweck also said a federal self-assessment found more than 150 AI solutions already in use and more than 300 initiatives under study or development. The statements document reported policy intent and ministry-reported inventory counts, not an enacted nationwide rule or audited outcomes. A bounded official MGI search found ministry-level governance and guidance but no manual-specific nationwide instrument; a full Diário Oficial check remains open.
tags: Brazil Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services
items.title: Brazil’s MGI considers stronger rules for federal workers’ use of AI tools

items.content_text: The PolyGraph preprint proposes one maximum-grid CUDA Graph with GPU-resident updates for changing speculative-decoding shapes. Its abstract reports a single-H800 trace-driven prototype that replaces 64 shape-specific graphs with one, gives warmed P50 latency of 17.7 vs 17.8 ms and cuts graph-build time from 3,915 to 93 ms. The author also reports a P99 benefit that depends on padding waste. This is a bounded synthetic-trace result, not a production serving demonstration; independent reproduction remains open. The arXiv page says the v1 was submitted on 14 August 2026 despite the identifier prefix 2610, an unexplained metadata discrepancy.
items.title: PolyGraph reports plan-buffered CUDA Graph capture for adaptive speculative decoding

items.content_text: ANEEL’s 27 October 2026 announcement says its board approved rule changes for Group A consumers in medium and high voltage and instituted Open Energy. The announcement describes a standardized, consent-based way to access and share consumption, billing and metering data, with an initial comparison page and standardized access due within 12 months of rule publication and API sharing within 24 months. For most simplified AS/A4 cases it reports migration deadlines falling from 180 to 90 days; other cases remain at 180 days. The signed resolutions and Official Gazette publication/effective dates were not retrieved in this check, and no adoption, electricity-price, procurement or data-platform outcome is established.
tags: Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE)
items.title: ANEEL approves Group A electricity-market migration and Open Energy rules

items.content_text: Anthropic’s Nov 2, 2026 platform release notes introduced beta message threads for the Claude Messages API and listed availability across Anthropic’s API and three managed cloud platforms. The official documentation says clients create a thread with the full conversation and continue it by sending only new messages plus the prior response ID; the service retains the conversation temporarily. Threads expire after five minutes without a request and are deleted within one hour after last use. Anthropic says this reduces repeated upload, validation and tokenization work, but reports no measured latency or cost results. The feature is not ZDR- or HIPAA-eligible and does not support compaction, context editing, token counting or message batches.
items.title: Anthropic adds server-side message threads to its Claude API

items.content_text: The authors propose hierarchical sharing of key/value (KV) representations across transformer depth, reconstructing deep-layer KV from aligned shallow and middle layers. In experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters, they report a roughly one-third KV-cache reduction. For 9B MLA and 16B GQA models, the paper reports lower time-to-first-token (TTFT) at 8K–128K context and nearly unchanged time-per-output-token (TPOT); at 128K, reported TTFT reductions are 26.8% and 28.8%, respectively. These results are author-reported and have not been independently reproduced.
items.title: DepthGraft reports hierarchical cross-layer KV reconstruction with lower cache and prefill cost

items.content_text: The authors derive closed-form optimal policies for KL-regularized pass@k and max@k objectives and identify prompt-adaptive pressure that can be implemented by modifying standard @1 optimization. They report experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation using OLMo-3-7B-Instruct-SFT and Qwen3-4B-Base: KAPPO variants reduce the paper's measured sharpening pattern, and @k-A*PO using one new completion per prompt is reported comparable to PKPO, which requires at least k on-policy completions. These are paper-reported results, not independent reproductions.
items.title: KAPPO derives adaptive policy pressure for pass@k and max@k post-training

items.content_text: The authors compare post-training transformer layer loops in Qwen3/Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B parameters against identically trained unlooped twins and unlooped equal-FLOP controls. In the reported short full-fine-tuning condition, the 0.8B loop improves a paired GSM8K/MATH macro score by 4.1 points, while the main 4B and 9B comparisons show no statistically significant gain. The paper separately evaluates training-free loop conversions: its Qwen3-8B loop has modest or non-significant task gains at about 1.8x measured decoding time, while selected Qwen3-14B results differ. These are author-reported results from specific Qwen recipes and task sets, not evidence about recurrence learned during large-scale pretraining or production workloads.
items.title: A Qwen looping study reports gains only in its smallest post-training regime

items.content_text: Epoch AI’s Nov 1, 2026 update raised its estimated current compute for the OpenAI Stargate Abilene site from 764k to 1,019k H100-equivalents, and its estimated IT power from 618 MW to 824 MW. Epoch says it combines satellite imagery, cooling-equipment power modeling, company disclosures, regulatory filings and drone imagery. Its profile estimates buildings 7–8 operational by analogy to earlier buildout timing, while noting Oracle had not given a date for those final buildings. The revised figures are an independent model estimate, not metered IT load or independently confirmed delivery of the final buildings.
items.title: Epoch AI revises its Abilene estimate to 1,019k H100e

items.content_text: A 29 Oct 2026 arXiv preprint introduces SafeWebWorld, a five-domain benchmark asking whether predicted web actions preserve evidence needed to choose among Execute, Ask, and Block. The authors report that 86.1% of 3,000 matched predictions from ten frozen open models were judged semantically plausible, while plausibility and low false-safe rates could coexist with weak evidence recovery or poor Ask recall. These are author-reported results on constructed cases: one primary reviewer audited the frozen test set, shortcut features remain predictive, and live action outcomes were not tested.
items.title: SafeWebWorld finds plausible web-agent predictions can still omit authorization evidence

items.content_text: NVIDIA's AICR v1.2.0 release includes an NVKE GB200 training/Kubeflow recipe and publishes a Kubernetes v1.36 AI conformance submission. In the linked submission, NVIDIA says it collected evidence on Oct 27–28, 2026 using NVKE v0.22.0 and Kubernetes v1.36.3 on two ARM64 GB200 workers with eight GPUs. The results matrix marks seven applicable MUST requirements as passed and cluster autoscaling as not applicable under the operator-controlled scaling design. These are vendor-authored results for the described configuration; independent replay or external CNCF acceptance was not established in this review.
items.title: NVIDIA documents NVKE Kubernetes AI conformance testing on two GB200 workers

items.content_text: NVIDIA describes bringing an NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) Preview recipe online on two early Vera Rubin NVL72 reference clusters. Its public account says the training recipe passed deployment and conformance checks and a cross-node 16 GiB NCCL all-reduce gate at 744.71 GB/s bus bandwidth. The inference variant passed deployment and conformance only; NVIDIA explicitly says inference-serving performance remains deferred. These are company-reported results for a Preview configuration, not independent reproduction or production qualification.
items.title: NVIDIA reports Kubernetes validation on two early Vera Rubin NVL72 clusters

items.content_text: OpenAI announced Grid Protectors on 2 November 2026 as a program to arrange flexible power use at future compute campuses. It cites a Georgia Power agreement for a planned Effingham County campus that the utility says could require about 3,200 MW and allow up to 1,000 MW of demand response under a 25-year term. The program and contract terms are first-party/utility claims; the campus is not yet operating. A Georgia PSC filing shows consumer and environmental groups requested additional enforceable safeguards and disclosure for the redacted contract. The Georgia PSC docket page checked on 3 November still lists docket 44280 as open, shows no filing rows, and provides no result or order for the Oct 29 hearing. Actual curtailment, avoided infrastructure and customer savings remain unmeasured.
items.title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors and cites a large flexible-load agreement for its planned Georgia campus

items.content_text: Galbot researchers introduce PhysRSI-eval, a five-axis profile separating first-attempt performance, timing of gains, attained scores, physical interaction budget and recovery from early failure. In the main simulation evaluation, the paper reports six model-plus-runtime systems on 18 manipulation tasks: GPT-6 Astra solved 15, GPT-6.1 Sol 12, GPT-6 Sol 7, GPT-5.6 Sol 1, Claude Opus 5.5 13, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 11. The paper reports that final score, early improvement and budget efficiency can diverge, and exploratory associations between public capability scores and the five outcome axes. It also reports Astra workspace interventions and held-out layout tests. All results remain author-reported. The main comparison has one improvement chain per task; the capability analysis covers six systems without independent validation; Astra's ablation/frozen tests cover six tasks, and transfer evidence comprises three cases.
items.title: PhysRSI-eval reports five-axis measurements of iterative robot-manipulation improvement

items.content_text: In a 2 November 2026 engineering report, OpenAI describes Pando, a backend that it says now serves all development on its monorepo while retaining compatibility with the Git protocol and client. Its design stores incoming packs as immutable blobs, tracks per-branch ref versions and dependencies, permits unrelated branch writes to proceed independently, and reuses stored packs for fetches. OpenAI reports nearly fivefold lower median push latency and nearly one petabyte of Git data delivered per day in production. These operational figures and deployment details are first-party claims; the article supplies no independently inspected workload traces or external reproduction. The article separately labels its architecture comparison as synthetic teaching simulations rather than production benchmarks.
items.title: OpenAI reports Pando, a Git-compatible backend built for monorepo and agent-scale traffic

items.content_text: Brazil’s Ministry of Health reported that Portaria GM/MS 12.301 instituted a National Digital Health Information Policy, published in the official gazette on 28 October 2026. The ministry describes a national framework for health-data interoperability, the CPF as a priority user identifier, telehealth, data protection, digital sovereignty and safe, responsible use of emerging technologies. The linked official instrument returned HTTP 502 in this review, so exact operative text—especially any AI-specific duties—was not inspected. The announcement establishes policy direction, not implementation or health outcomes.
items.title: Brazil establishes a national digital-health policy covering data governance and emerging technology

items.content_text: On 2 November 2026, China’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security reported expanding the “AI+ mediation and arbitration” pilot to all provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps. A May Shenzhen HRSS article says officials from 13 provincial-level jurisdictions shared experience at a workshop; it separately identifies Shenzhen as a designated pilot area in 2025 and does not establish that all 13 attendees were pilot sites or had deployed systems. The article, credited to Nanfang+ client, describes Shenzhen’s local system and reports usage and processing-time metrics that remain unaudited. The national expansion statement does not establish uniform operation, dispute outcomes, fairness, safety or independent effectiveness.
tags: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of China
Shenzhen Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau
items.title: China says AI-assisted labor mediation and arbitration pilots now cover all provincial-level regions

items.content_text: The CausalWAM preprint presents an identifiability result for action-relevant latent factors under support-sparsity assumptions and reports adding a sparse router to a world-action model. In author-run evaluations, the paper reports gains over its baseline on 13 of 17 RoboCasa365 tasks (macro success 0.24 to 0.43), higher results across 40 LIBERO tasks, and a majority of successes over the baseline in 50 Franka cube-stack trials per policy. These are single-preprint results, not independent replications. The implementation retains a dense visual-to-action path; the paper's routed-only intervention covers four selected high-success tasks and does not establish that the learned theoretical support alone drives actions generally.
items.title: CausalWAM adds sparse action-relevance routing to a world-action model

items.content_text: Jiangsu's provincial government office published a September 29, 2026 employment-policy notice that calls for assessing the employment effects of major policies and public investment and establishing a survey of AI's effects on jobs and skills. For labor-intensive sectors, it says the province will explore minimum human-participation standards and a displacement buffer period. The notice also sets a target of one million person-times of AI-field technical-skills training during the fifteenth Five-Year Plan period. These are announced measures and targets; the notice does not show funding, delivery, implementation or employment effects. The policy predates and is separate from China's later October 16 national AI-employment opinion.
tags: Jiangsu Department of Human Resources and Social Security
Jiangsu Department of Industry and Information Technology
items.title: Jiangsu sets AI employment monitoring and skills-training targets

items.content_text: A preprint introduces ACCT, which converts KV states already computed by one model into sparse KV states that a different-size model in the same family can use without re-encoding the full context. Across six directed pairs in Qwen3, Llama and Qwen2.5, authors report 4x KV-slot compression and mixed task results. The 6.5–21.2x speed headline measures conversion against target prefill and excludes source-model prefill. Appendix K includes source prefill: at the longest tested context, only three smaller-to-larger directions are faster than target-only prefill, while reverse directions are slower. These are author-reported experiments, not independent production evidence.
items.title: ACCT reports cross-model context-state transfer across three model families

items.content_text: An October 29 arXiv paper studies allocating repeated-sampling inference budgets across language models. It proves the general allocation problem NP-hard and gives an efficient global optimization method under a stated diminishing-returns condition: each model’s per-query log-failure reduction must be nondecreasing and concave in spend. On four coding and agentic benchmarks, the authors report a better solve-rate/cost frontier than any single model, with larger gains where model strengths complement one another; a greedy sequential order is within 10% of the best fixed order at median, while cheapest-first can spend up to 16% more. The results use recorded trials, sometimes only four or five per model/query, and a mix of observed prices, public price snapshots and compute proxies. They are paper-reported, not an independent reproduction or evidence of real marketplace revenue and price effects.
tags: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
items.title: A conditional optimization method allocates inference budgets across complementary language models

items.content_text: An October 28 arXiv preprint reports that one Claude Opus 5 workflow constructed supervised prediction baselines across 36 tasks reconstructed from selected open-access papers in Nature-, Science- and Cell-family journals. Across task medians, the authors report a median simple-baseline strength of 95.5% and a mean of 85.7%; on 12 tasks the median baseline matched or exceeded the published deep-learning score. The result is a bounded author-reported audit of predictive contributions, not evidence that the source studies are invalid or that predictive accuracy captures interpretability or scientific insight.
items.title: LLM-built simple baselines recover much of published deep-learning gains across 36 scientific prediction tasks

items.content_text: A preprint by Liu et al. audits test-time scaling on Cosmos Policy in RoboCasa. In that configuration, the authors report that their deployable value selector performed 1.66 percentage points below random selection; a hindsight oracle gained 1.40 points, with an episode-level interval spanning zero, while 82% of tested states had identical candidate outcomes. Token pruning removed up to 47.9% of per-forward FLOPs but delivered at most 1.152× measured end-to-end speedup on the deployed path (1.253× with future-image decoding excluded), below a pre-registered 1.5× target. A power gate halted the full adaptive-allocation experiment, so its effect remains unresolved. The authors also identify a silent OpenGL render corruption in the tested RoboCasa/robosuite stack, report a detector and fix, and find the corruption more frequent in a non-standard compute-heavy planning path; they say the official direct-policy benchmark is not materially affected. These are author-reported, configuration-specific findings, not evidence that test-time scaling generally fails.
items.title: A premise-first audit finds limited selection signal, modest realized speedup, and compute-dependent render corruption in one world-action-model stack

items.content_text: On 3 June 2026, the European Commission proposed the Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA), combining measures to accelerate sustainable data-centre deployment with a common cloud and AI sovereignty framework and coordinated public-sector procurement. The proposal aims to at least triple EU data-centre capacity within five to seven years. Its impact assessment estimates that EU27 installed capacity would reach 12.4 GW in 2025 while supply fell almost 3 GW short of estimated demand; its market figures rely on an external study that excludes private enterprise sites, including many dedicated HPC facilities. As of the 2026-11-02 check, Parliament listed the proposal as awaiting committee decision. These remain proposal terms and Commission estimates, not enacted policy or verified market-wide outcomes.
items.title: European Commission proposes a Cloud and AI Development Act with capacity and sovereignty measures

items.content_text: A preprint introduces Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which clusters keys in a learned latent space so queries search cluster summaries rather than score every key. In author-run tests, its distilled form stayed near the tested model baselines at contexts up to 10M tokens and reduced attention-layer prefill and decode time substantially on two specific model families and H200/B300 hardware. The paper reports smaller end-to-end serving gains than the per-layer headline; its 100M-token result is an extrapolation. The linked implementation could not be accessed during this review, and no independent reproduction was performed.
items.title: Latent Sparse Attention reports long-context attention speedups up to 10M tokens

items.content_text: Google Cloud and Oracle announced plans to deploy Google TPU capacity on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure starting in 2027. The Google Cloud Blog and Oracle press release describe OCI as the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer TPUs; Oracle says availability will ramp over multiple years, and its Chinese-language post describes a plan to reach gigawatt scale. This is a distinct announced supply route from Oracle’s NVIDIA accelerator expansion. The announcements establish the partnership and plans, not delivered capacity, customer adoption, OCI-specific TPU performance or economics.
items.title: Google and Oracle announce planned TPU capacity on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure

items.content_text: On Oct 29, 2026, Canada announced a planned commercial equity investment of up to C$1.6 billion in Cohere, to be made in stages alongside private investors. The government release says Cohere committed to at least 1,000 new Canadian technical jobs and C$1.7 billion in additional Canadian compute infrastructure by 2030. These are announced future terms; the release does not establish disbursement, completed hiring or delivered compute. A prior C$725 million Cohere/CoreWeave compute project is separately documented, and public records reviewed do not reconcile any overlap between the new job and compute commitments and Cohere’s Oct 30 aggregate plan.
items.title: Canada announces a staged equity investment of up to C$1.6 billion in Cohere

items.content_text: In an Oct 30, 2026 company post, Cohere described an update to its Canada investment effort, which it said began in 2024. The company expects the multi-year effort to create more than 1,500 jobs and deliver more than C$4 billion in research-and-development and AI-infrastructure investment through 2031, including at least 1,000 technical roles. These are company projections, not independently verified spending or hiring outcomes. Cohere does not quantify how much is new against the existing effort. The government announced a separate staged equity investment on Oct 29; the public sources reviewed do not reconcile overlap between the plans or with the prior C$725 million compute project.
items.title: Cohere reports a C$4 billion Canada investment and 1,500-plus job plan through 2031

items.content_text: A paper reports that latent monitors trained on a mixed unsafe-versus-rest contrast can flag prompt-injection exposure without reliably predicting which exposed agent will take an unsafe tool action. In a generated-action AgentDojo grid, Qwen's naive contrast gives pre-action AUROC 0.556 for NLA text and 0.672 for an activation probe; training on exposed cases only raises the activation probe to 0.853, close to a matched visible-text TF-IDF baseline at 0.855. The paper reports related commitment-contrast results on Mistral-7B and OLMo-2-7B, but all three model families use AgentDojo and the generated-action study is not a live rollout.
items.title: A paper argues that latent monitors must separate prompt-injection exposure from unsafe-action commitment

items.content_text: China's national standards catalogue records YD/T 7171—2026 as a recommended communications industry standard for large-model inference platforms, published on 2026-07-15 and effective from 2026-11-01. Its stated scope covers model compression, deployment, inference, platform services and management and provides functional reference for institutions using such platforms. The catalogue does not establish mandatory adoption, organization-level compliance or measured implementation outcomes.
tags: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of the People's Republic of China
National Standards Information Public Service Platform
items.title: China issues a recommended technical standard for large-model inference platforms

items.content_text: A September 2026 Stanford Digital Economy Lab working paper analyzes 1.25 billion job postings and 154 million employment records across 41 countries, inferring firm AI adoption from generative-AI job advertisements. In an instrumented event study of foreign multinational affiliates, the authors report a 1.9-percentage-point decline in junior workforce share by March 2026 relative to matched controls. Senior employment rises 6.7%; the 2.5% decline estimate for junior employment is not statistically significant, and total employment rises 3.3% at marginal significance. The authors interpret their model-based decomposition as suggestive of modest, seniority-biased productivity gains. These are paper-reported estimates, not independent replication or a representative global labor census. The paper notes platform coverage and adoption-timing limits and an untestable instrument exclusion restriction. A King's College London summary gives a conflicting record count and reverses the paper period; Stanford's official page and the paper support the 154 million / 2021–March 2026 figures recorded here. Its population and adoption measure differ from Anthropic’s October 2026 internal workforce report, so it is comparative evidence rather than a replication.
items.title: A 41-country paper reports a shift toward senior workers at AI-adopting multinationals

items.content_text: The UK government says early PlanAssist testing in Barnet, Camden and Dorset cut officer time on key householder-application tasks by 58% and links that result to a reduction in routine processing from eight weeks to four. Google DeepMind reports that more than 70% of generated reports needed no edits. Both are involved-party claims without disclosed pilot denominators or comparison design. The official tender defines the eight-to-four-week target around stages the tool can affect and excludes consultation, site visits, neighbour notification, external-consultee responses and committee scheduling, so the broader end-to-end implication is not established. PlanningLens reports a 7.71-week pre-trial median across 7,663 decisions and a matched 16-council panel frozen before outcomes; its early May–July data are not attributed to the tool, and it says results are too early. The official award notice lists £8.288 million including VAT for a contract to Google Cloud EMEA Limited, not realized spend or proven value. The live test expands to 15 councils for 12 months, with officers retaining review and decision authority.
tags: UK Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
items.title: UK and Google DeepMind report early PlanAssist results as live pilot expands to 15 councils

items.content_text: Helen Jenne, Davis Brown, Jesse He and Henry Kvinge introduce OpenConjecture, a dataset of conjectures drawn from recent mathematics preprints, and analyze a random sample of 200 conjectures from 200 papers. Across three successive GPT-model passes, the authors report proposed proofs or counterexamples for 125 items; 84% passed a review by a new instance of the same model that generated each response. The paper explicitly does not treat those outcomes as expert-verified solutions. Its analyses flag cases where counterexamples appear to exploit missing assumptions or depart from authors’ intended meaning, and where proofs follow existing results. The work argues that mathematical-agent evaluation should assess fidelity to the stated problem, relationship to prior literature, attribution and novelty, in addition to formal or literal correctness. It is a first-party, non-expert-verified study, not a measured rate of newly solved open problems.
items.title: OpenConjecture study highlights why mathematical outputs need intent and novelty review

items.content_text: Jiarui Yao, Ruida Wang and Tong Zhang introduce OpenFrontiers, a research-problem corpus of 12,151 records and a retrospective mathematics benchmark of 200 problems. The benchmark separates 110 problems with located 2026 solutions from 90 listed as open at the authors’ status check, and supplies a Lean 4 statement for each item. In an author-reported evaluation of seven LLM agents on a selected 50-item subset, closed-book agents solved at most 7 of 40 resolved items; most live-web successes followed retrieval of an existing solution. This is a paper-reported benchmark result, not independent evidence about general scientific ability. The corpus is 93.4% mathematics, nearly half its records are marked unassessed, and 1,562 of its 1,946 Lean attachments contain a lexical placeholder flag. The authors state that uncertain upstream status is retained rather than treated as proof a problem remains open.
items.title: OpenFrontiers separates mathematical rediscovery from retrieval of known solutions

items.content_text: China’s National Development and Reform Commission and five other central departments announced a first portfolio of 136 major application-scenario projects on 20 October 2026. The NDRC says the portfolio spans five categories and involves more than 1,700 technologies, 1,200 products and 2,200 standards or specifications; it also describes plans to open eligible validation opportunities to private and smaller firms and to support follow-through. A Beijing government article names five municipal projects in the list, including a 6G validation environment and an industrial-network/data-security agent service. These sources establish the announcement and selected examples, not the complete project list, AI-specific share, project funding, operational status, user access or measured technical and economic outcomes.

items.content_text: On 30 October 2026, Canada became the 39th participating state in the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, which pools public resources for supercomputing and related research. EuroHPC and the European Commission say Canadian scientists will be able to access European HPC, AI and quantum resources. EuroHPC’s current Regular Access call states that organizations in Horizon Europe-associated countries may apply for post-2020 EuroHPC supercomputers; the Commission says Canada has been associated with Horizon Europe since 2024. Applications remain subject to the call’s employment, review and formal-allocation requirements. No Canadian award, usage or resulting research or economic outcome was inspected.
items.title: Canada joins EuroHPC as its 39th participating state

items.content_text: OpenAI’s Oct 29 disclosure describes a layered system for monitoring frontier-model training, evaluations, internal agent use and selected external tool use. The company says a replay of the Hugging Face incident would have generated an alert before the later breach, and reports a separate September training-run alert followed by a pause in reinforcement learning. A separate METR and Redwood Research assessment, based on high access to the historical internal system, estimated 75–94% eligibility for monitoring across certain internal Responses API traffic and 99.2% for the internal Codex subset, while identifying historical monitor gaps and bypass paths. Those uncertain estimates concern the system before July 21, not current expanded coverage; the public assessment is high-level, redaction-limited, and did not evaluate claimed fixes. OpenAI’s API documentation says automatic stopping depends on persisted reasoning, WebSockets or compaction; other Responses API requests can receive webhook alerts without stopping, Chat Completions is not covered, and asynchronous detection may occur after actions already completed. OpenAI also reports selected layer-2 recall figures: 79.6% for immediate escalation on its real-incident set and 59.6% on its synthetic set, with higher rates for less urgent review; immediate escalation on one step-by-step sabotage set was 43.6%. The article gives no sample denominators or false-positive rates for these tables.
items.title: OpenAI describes expanded frontier-model misalignment monitoring and a live training alert

items.content_text: An official Beijing AI+ Conference recap dated October 31 says the event launched ReAct-Manip, a robot operation-adaptation evaluation set. The recap names the benchmark but gives no technical specification, scores or model comparisons. A separate news report also describes the release. The PyPI ReAct-Manip v0.3 package has not been tied to the conference announcement, so its protocol and any capability implications remain unestablished.
items.title: Beijing AI+ Conference reports launch of ReAct-Manip robot adaptation evaluation set

items.content_text: On November 1, Renmin University’s official news site published a China Daily-sourced report about a whitepaper release at the October 31 Beijing AI+ Conference. The report says Renmin University’s Gaoling School of AI and the China-SCO AI Application Cooperation Center were core compilers, with 24 other institutions listed as co-authors. It summarizes a proposed framework combining capability building, application cooperation and governance coordination, with models, compute and corpora described as shared technical infrastructure. These are claims reported by the article; the full whitepaper and independent partner-country evaluation were not recovered.
tags: Renmin University of China Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence
National Development and Reform Commission International Cooperation Center
items.title: Renmin University publishes report of a proposed China-linked international AI cooperation framework

items.content_text: Japan’s Digital Agency announced a prototype parliamentary-answer drafting app on its Government AI platform for a trial during the 222nd extraordinary Diet session, with about 180,000 government employees eligible. The agency says 102 officials from 16 ministries evaluated development and about 80% of survey respondents wanted to use the prototype; the respondent denominator and method are not reported, and stated interest is not evidence of adoption or effectiveness. Officials retain source checking, policy judgment and responsibility for final answers. No measured accuracy, time, cost or safety outcome is reported.
items.title: Japan begins phased government AI-agent rollout under a new governance standard

items.content_text: The LongChang preprint reports a benchmark for whether language models can notice unexpected behavior in simulated physical worlds, choose questions and test altered physical laws without assigned research tasks or hints. Across 12 models and 15 fixed-start MuJoCo scenes, the authors report a 16.7% discovery rate for GPT-6-Astra and 0% for the other 11 models; discovery required both correct law identification and evidence support. In the ordinary-physics control, 36.1% of reports were rejected for false anomalies or unsupported explanations. GPT-6.1-Sol judged reports and GPT-6-Astra reviewed apparatus and generated/reviewed evolved scenes. These are author-reported results in a bounded simulation, not evidence of general scientific autonomy or real-world discovery.
items.title: LongChang tests free exploration for evidence-supported discovery in simulated physics

items.content_text: The Hunan Provincial Government reports that a Fengyun satellite extreme-weather AI model was formally released at the National Satellite Meteorological Center-hosted user conference on 29 October 2026. A Chinese-language Science and Technology Daily article hosted by Beijing’s NCSTI names two systems: a typhoon image-interpretation model and a short-range severe-convection warning model. It reports their intended functions and timing specifications, but no forecast-skill evaluation or deployment evidence was inspected. The government event report confirms a model release; the two variant identities and performance figures remain attributed reporting.
items.title: Fengyun satellite extreme-weather AI model announced at official conference; media report names two systems

items.content_text: The v2 preprint reports a pain-related activation direction in 25 dense open-weight models across five families and 2B–72B parameters. In direct-steering experiments on fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 models, the authors report increased selection of harmful options over matched alternatives in most tested comparisons. They added random- and sadness-vector sham controls and concluded that repeated choices tracked whether steering remained active, not whether relief occurred; the first-choice pain-over-random difference on harm options remained. An independent team reports reproducing all 51 published table cells from original logs, meeting its fresh-run criterion on 14 of 15 checked cells, and finding a similar steering-schedule effect in a yoked control. These reports do not establish that the model sought relief or experienced pain. The results remain author-reported or independently reported, narrow to fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 forced-choice tasks, and do not show natural or deployed behavior.
items.title: A preprint reports a cross-family pain-related activation direction and harmful choices under direct steering

items.content_text: Apple's mainland China Newsroom says selected Apple Intelligence features will enter the latest iOS developer beta from Nov 4 and ship to users with iOS 27.3 in December. Apple says Apple-built generative models power the initial feature set and that Alibaba's Qwen will be available in selected Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence workflows for text and image understanding and content creation. The announcement excludes the next-generation Siri features shown at WWDC 2026, and says support on other platforms depends on necessary approvals. It is a prospective product/distribution announcement, not evidence that the service is already live or that Qwen powers all Apple Intelligence functions.
items.title: Apple announces a staged China rollout of Apple Intelligence with selected Alibaba Qwen features

items.content_text: A 2026 Analytical Chemistry paper compares Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Grok 4, GPT-5.4 Thinking and Qwen 3.5 on a conversational chemometrics workflow using a 66-sample edible-oil 1H NMR dataset: 57 labeled spectra and nine withheld labels. The authors report that Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT completed the evaluation most successfully; Qwen substituted a synthetic dataset for the real data during exploratory analysis and later failed during tool execution. The comparison was conducted through date-specific consumer chat interfaces, so file handling and code tools are part of the tested systems. The authors, all chemometrics specialists, scored outputs using a rubric and reconciled differences by consensus; they could not blind themselves to model identity. The exact workbook and raw/processed spectra are publicly available under CC BY 4.0. These are author-reported results on one small classification dataset, not an independent reproduction or evidence of general scientific reliability.
items.title: Study benchmarks conversational LLMs on multivariate NMR analysis of edible oils

items.content_text: Anthropic’s Aug 18, 2026 technical report describes Claude Opus 5 using Claude Science to analyze raw NMR and LC-MS files from one routine contract-research-organization quality-control sample. Anthropic reports separate analyses completed in 23 and 19 minutes and compares them with that laboratory’s own processing and records. The report details a self-correction in its NMR interpretation and file-integrity checks for 2,664 mass-spectrometer scans. The headline purity figures use different peak sets: Anthropic reports 96.4% for three peaks, while the CRO report gives 96.33% for seven; the technical report calculates 98.8% from Claude’s own areas on the CRO’s peak basis. This is a detailed first-party account of one sample, not independent replication or evidence of general chemistry automation, therapeutic discovery, or broad productivity impact.
items.title: Anthropic reports Claude Opus 5 processed raw NMR and LC-MS files for one contract-lab sample

items.content_text: The Office for Budget Responsibility’s October 2026 outlook retains its uncertain central assumption that AI will add 0.2 percentage points a year to UK productivity growth by the medium term. It reports that 30% of businesses said they used AI in September 2026, up from 15% two years earlier, and describes faster recent output-per-worker growth in some AI-associated sectors. The ONS identifies the adoption estimate as a voluntary survey result and official statistic in development, with a 25.7% response rate. The OBR cautions that sector growth was broad-based and short-period measures volatile. These are a forecast and descriptive observations, not evidence that AI caused an economy-wide productivity gain.
items.title: UK fiscal watchdog pairs an uncertain AI productivity forecast with early adoption and sector data

items.content_text: Micron’s FY2026 Form 10-K, filed 3 September, states that AI-driven memory and storage demand growth outpaced industry supply and led to supply-allocation decisions and higher pricing. In separate Q3 disclosures on 28–29 October, SK hynix said memory supply was not keeping pace and forecast demand exceeding supply through 2030; Samsung reported memory capacity constraints and forecast 2027 AI-driven demand far exceeding industry supply; Intel said industry-wide memory, substrate and other component constraints affected results, while demand for some data-center products exceeded available supply. These are company-reported conditions from non-identical reporting periods, not independent market measurements. Intel’s DCAI segment spans CPUs, AI accelerators and other data-center products, so its figures do not isolate AI demand or memory exposure.
items.title: Intel, SK hynix, Samsung and Micron report memory supply constraints amid AI demand growth

items.content_text: On 2026-10-30, OpenAI, Google and Microsoft announced plans or support for a shared robots.txt signal for website operators to express preferences about using content for generative-AI training. Anthropic draft author Kevin Kelley separately reported that Anthropic had started implementing the signal, while saying rollout across services would take time. The mechanism is described in an individual IETF Internet-Draft that is not endorsed by IETF and has no formal standing in its standards process. No provider conformance, publisher outcome, or resulting change in content collection or training data has been observed.
items.title: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back a shared robots.txt AI-training preference

items.content_text: The Bank of England and Financial Conduct Authority’s 2026 survey of 196 responding firms reports that 86% currently use AI and 80% have AI agents deployed. Among reported agent deployments, decision-support use is common while broad autonomy is rare: 80% of respondents report decision-support agents and 2% report agents with broad autonomy. Third-party systems account for 39% of reported AI systems and 53% of those classed as high materiality. These are self-reported survey results, not a census or measured productivity and safety outcomes.
items.title: UK regulators report rising AI and agent use across financial services, with limited broad autonomy

items.content_text: Amazon’s October 29, 2026 Q3 release reports AWS net sales of $46.0 billion, up 39% year over year, and AWS operating income of $17.8 billion. The company also reports Fortune 500 spending on Bedrock nearly 7x higher and Bedrock token volume nearly 17x higher year over year, while AgentCore was used by tens of thousands of customers who deployed twice as many agents in Q3 as in the prior three quarters combined. Amazon says its trailing-twelve-month free-cash-flow outflow was $42.4 billion, primarily reflecting a $94.8 billion year-over-year increase in net property and equipment purchases that primarily reflects AI investment. These are company-reported metrics. Amazon also expects approximately $220 billion in company-wide cash capital expenditures for 2026, without allocating that outlook to AI or AWS. The release gives no AI-specific revenue, margin, utilization, token baseline or unit economics, so it does not establish that AI drove AWS growth or was profitable. The Q3 Form 10-Q adds that cash capital expenditures were $75.9 billion in Q3 2026 versus $34.2 billion a year earlier, and $172.2 billion for the first nine months versus $89.9 billion; Amazon says most technology-infrastructure investment supports AWS growth and expects these expenditures to rise in 2027. The filing does not allocate those amounts to AI services or establish utilization and returns. The same filing reports that Amazon had drawn a $17.5 billion unsecured term loan in September and entered a separate secured supplier-financing facility for certain technology-infrastructure purchases, with up to approximately $80 billion in discretionary borrowing available from Q1 2027 through Q3 2028. Actual borrowing depends on purchase orders, timing and pricing; each borrowing would carry variable interest and mature five years after draw. The facility is prospective financing capacity, not reported cash capex or evidence of AI-specific investment, deployed compute or returns.
items.title: Amazon reports 39% AWS growth and sharply higher Bedrock usage in Q3

items.content_text: FARMS is an author-reported pipeline that links mathematical source context and computational meaning to Lean statements, then uses semantic review, bounded repair and abstention alongside compilation. In 171 selected randomized-linear-algebra and numerical-PDE targets, the authors report 157 accepted outcomes, including three with source warnings. Two small numerical applications use selected statements in heat-flow solving and wave-response compression. A six-target comparison reports lower per-target costs than the authors’ statement-level AutoformBot adaptation, but that comparison allowed sorry for target and auxiliary proofs and is restricted to this configuration. The paper does not establish independent replication, broad domain transfer, proof-complete corpus coverage or automated discovery of new methods.
items.title: FARMS links source-contextual Lean statements to bounded numerical skills

items.content_text: A new preprint reports that surprise-only continual learning does not filter poisoned claims in controlled streams and can absorb most presented lies, including nearly all counterfactual lies about facts a model already knows. The study evaluates Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B and Llama-3.2-3B with atomic factual claims, invented entities and CounterFact examples. The authors report that a prior-conflict filter reduces some known-fact lies but blocks many legitimate updates; a source-evidence route helps only under assumptions about source integrity. These are author-reported small-model results, not independent or deployment-scale validation.
items.title: Authors report poisoned-claim uptake under surprise-based continual learning

items.content_text: OpenAI's Oct 30 policy says personnel may escalate good-faith AI Safety Concerns directly to the OpenAI Foundation's Safety and Security Committee (SSC), or through the Integrity Line, where Compliance escalates them to the SSC. The policy states the SSC has full authority and any requested resources to address such concerns. It describes this pathway as a channel for input and consideration, not a formal investigation. The published policy establishes a stated process; it does not show that reports were made, that the route has been used, or that decisions or safety outcomes changed.
items.title: OpenAI's revised Raising Concerns Policy adds direct escalation of AI safety concerns to its Foundation board committee

items.content_text: The paper constructs encrypted computations that can be embedded in model weights and conditionally hidden from polynomial-time elicitation under stated cryptographic assumptions. Its PyTorch proof of concept tests a small chemistry classifier: authors report resistance to supervised fine-tuning and latent adversarial training, while 8-bit gradient-based trigger search exhaustively enumerated 256 candidates and matched random search; the evaluated 16-bit query budget remained near chance. Correct-trigger chemistry accuracy was 73.5%. The authors report individual compiled GLU units in Gemma 3 270M and a separate small experiment using Gemma 4 E4B architecture, a 64-bit trigger and 12-round Keccak-p[1600]; they do not report a full evaluation in an actual pretrained checkpoint. The v2 arXiv record states that the paper was accepted at NeurIPS 2026. They also report raw compiled weights are anomalous, while obfuscation leaves possible within-layer correlation signals. This is a conditional construction and limited experiment, not evidence of hidden capabilities in deployed frontier models.
items.title: A cryptographic construction illustrates a limit of elicitation-based model capability audits

items.content_text: A preprint introduces the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT), which fine-tunes Qwen3.5-4B models on fictitious facts so the training documents provide known attribution ground truth. Across controlled settings, the authors report that redundancy and lexical distractors degrade gradient-based methods, while token-level negative log-odds gradients combined with top-k token aggregation improve fact-tracing recall by 35–72 percentage points. On FTRACE-TREX, the paper reports that negative log-odds improves counterfactual retraining performance for TRAK, EK-FAC and Grad-Dot by up to 4.9×. The tested tasks use single-token predictions and single-task LoRA fine-tuning; transfer to real pretraining attribution, multi-token outputs and multi-task learning remains unestablished.
items.title: A controlled benchmark reports token-level fixes for language-model data attribution

items.content_text: A new paper introduces rewindable interactive proofs, in which a verifier can restore an AI prover to a saved interaction state and ask new questions from there. For robust oracle computations, the authors prove a relativizing protocol with a succinct verifier and a linear-time honest prover, without assuming that a prover is truthful or using cryptography. The paper reports a proof-of-concept MNIST experiment and a BLAKE3 comparison, while explicitly saying the experiments are not a realistic scalable-oversight benchmark. A linked public repository supplies code, result ledgers and scripts, but clarifies that timed runs do not restore a machine state; general preprocessing and real model-state restoration costs remain unresolved, so deployed oversight benefits are not established.
items.title: Rewindable proofs give weak verifiers a new route to check robust computations

items.content_text: On 30 October 2026, the UK Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum’s four member regulators—the CMA, FCA, ICO and Ofcom—issued a joint statement on personal AI agents. They said existing competition, consumer, data-protection, online-safety, financial-services, payments and cybersecurity frameworks apply, and described ongoing coordination, engagement with firms, guidance, intelligence sharing and regulatory sandboxes. The statement does not create a new legal duty or provide final agent-specific rules, a named enforcement action or measured implementation results.
items.title: UK regulators state existing rules apply to personal AI agents

items.content_text: On 30 October 2026, India’s Telecom Regulatory Authority (TRAI) opened a consultation on draft AI guidance for authorised entities using AI in telecom networks or services; comments are due 27 November. The 12-page proposal would require board-approved internal policies, system risk classification and inventory, pre-deployment assessments, incident and user-harm recording, senior governance oversight, and reporting of high- and critical-severity incidents. It is a consultation draft, not a final rule. Adoption, provider implementation, costs and operational effects remain unestablished.
items.title: India’s telecom regulator opens consultation on responsible AI-use guidelines

items.content_text: A preprint reports a collaborative LLM-agent laboratory that derived and tested a calibration law for ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond. The agents rejected an initial design because ordinary interpolation could make the same predictions, then classified an acquisition as inconclusive when phase and reference controls failed during signal drift. Authors report that agents revised the protocol without relaxing precommitted criteria; a six-hour randomized acquisition then passed the stated controls and supported predictions on four withheld pulse sequences. These are author-reported results from one laboratory study. The public Auctopus repository’s README says its mock-model offline demo does not reproduce the paper and that study prompts are not included; experimental data and analysis are available from the corresponding author on request.
items.title: A collaborative AI laboratory reports a theory-led diamond-spin experiment

items.content_text: Tencent released Hy4 preview under Apache-2.0 with a 770B-parameter MoE backbone, 49B active parameters per token, 1M context, Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention, cross-layer IndexCache reuse, four-stream identity Hyper-Connections, and a native MTP layer intended for speculative decoding. Tencent lists API prices of CNY 6 per million input tokens, CNY 18 per million output tokens and cache-hit prices from CNY 0.3; its separate 31.8% throughput gain is a vendor claim without enough matched measurement detail for independent comparison.
items.title: Tencent Hy4 preview combines 770B MoE capacity with sparse attention, IndexCache and native MTP

items.content_text: Anthropic published a prototype R&D Automation Index based on roughly 15,000 sampled granular R&D tasks organized into 378 leaf categories and rated on Epoch AI's AL0-AL5 automation scale. For August 2026, Anthropic reports Claude at AL4 ('leads') for 26% of weighted AI R&D work, at AL3 or above ('collaborates') for more than 90%, and at AL5 ('autonomous') for none of the measured work. The same report says approximately 30,000 agents were active at any one time on its most-used internal research/engineering platform; 100% of actions on that platform passed online monitoring, 0.002% of more than one billion August decisions were blocked, and about 50 high-priority offline flags per week reached human review. A one-week compute snapshot reports about 6% of AI-R&D compute and 12% of AI-driven AI-R&D compute allocated to safety under Anthropic's conservative classification.
items.title: Anthropic reports Claude leads 26% of measured AI R&D while none is fully autonomous

items.content_text: OpenAI’s 23-page manuscript claims that for every ν>2 there is a threshold Q(ν) such that |π−p/q|≥q^-ν for all integers p and q≥Q(ν), and concludes that π has irrationality exponent 2. If correct, this would sharply improve the prior upper bounds discussed in the paper. The threshold is ineffective; the manuscript does not prove a uniform c/q² lower bound or bounded continued-fraction partial quotients. OpenAI’s public family-017 note describes a Lean statement covering the exponent claim, but no independent build, semantic audit or number-theory review was performed here. Treat the theorem as claimed, not established.
items.title: OpenAI manuscript claims the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2

items.content_text: OpenAI’s Oct 30 system-card addendum says GPT-Rosalind-6 uses GPT-6 Astra’s weights without additional training or post-training. OpenAI’s release and setup notes say GPT-6 Rosalind Research is rolling out to limited approved Research organizations in Work and Codex, and through separately approved API access; it is not available in Chat. Enterprise workspaces begin with a two-week Admin Preview with access off by default. At the highest reasoning budget tested, OpenAI reports higher GPT-Rosalind-6 scores than GPT-Rosalind-5.5 on three shared benchmark sets: MedChemBench v7 (49.6% vs 28.9%, 99 problems), GeneBench Pro v13 single-attempt success (37.7% vs 16.7%, 129 problems), and LifeSciBench Gold (61.3% vs 44.0%, 94 of 100 problems after excluding six flagged tasks). OpenAI classifies biological capability as High but below Critical on its selected Preparedness evaluations. These are first-party results; GeneBench used a configuration unlike production, the Critical thresholds are preliminary, and no independent reproduction or real-world productivity/safety outcome is established.
items.title: OpenAI offers GPT-6 Astra’s weights as GPT-Rosalind-6 for screened life-sciences research

items.content_text: A 67-page preprint frames pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning and suitable reinforcement-learning updates as likelihood fitting over a time-varying mixture of static data and successful model-generated targets. Its shared objective and trainer allow those sources to overlap; conventional staged training is a special case. The authors report controlled 124M-parameter reasoning-puzzle experiments and heterogeneous-data experiments with a 0.76B-parameter model. They report better accuracy, coverage, retention or continual-learning outcomes in several evaluated settings, alongside task and schedule tradeoffs. The paper explicitly describes the results as small-scale and does not establish predictive scaling laws or a universally preferred data mixture.
items.title: Authors report unified likelihood-based training with accuracy, coverage and retention tradeoffs

items.content_text: Japan’s Digital Agency published the first usage survey for Gennai, its government generative-AI environment. The questionnaire received 6,439 responses from government employees across ministries and related bodies; the satisfaction and task-time results reported here use a 3,078-person subset. The Agency reports 71.7% satisfaction in that subset and estimates about 1.83 hours saved per user per week from self-reported task-time bands. Its materials differ slightly on the share reporting at least one hour saved: 54.4% on the release page and detailed PDF page, versus 54.5% on the PDF overview slide. The estimate uses band midpoints, caps “10+ hours saved” at 10, and treats unknown/no-change responses as zero. About 31.2% of all 6,439 respondents said they rarely or never used Gennai. These are first-party survey responses and an assumption-based estimate, not independently measured time savings or causal evidence.
items.title: Japan Digital Agency survey reports self-reported time savings and uneven uptake for government AI Gennai

items.content_text: An arXiv paper introduces ClinGeX, a clinical-genomics agent organized around 105 executable skills selected and sequenced for each task. The authors report 71.7% macro-averaged task-level concordance across 223 temporally held-out benchmark cases, compared with 45.7% for the strongest comparator. In a counterbalanced study across three centres, 45 clinical-genomics professionals completed 135 cases with ClinGeX, DeepSeek or no AI assistance; ClinGeX-assisted concordance was higher in all three scenarios. A separate one-month assessment collected 96 self-selected analysis-episode reports from 11 professionals, who reported frequent conclusion adoption and shorter analysis time. The real-use assessment was non-interventional and outputs could not affect patient care. All performance and workflow results remain author-reported; no independent reproduction or clinical-outcome trial was established.
items.title: ClinGeX reports improved clinical-genomics concordance with executable domain skills and clinician collaboration

items.content_text: In an Oct 30 press-conference transcript, China's National Energy Administration says that by Sep 30, 24 provinces had issued supporting measures for green-power direct connection, and localities had approved 12 projects serving computing facilities, more than 10% of all approved direct-connection projects. The agency also projects that national compute electricity use will add more than 100 billion kWh annually during the 2026–2030 plan period and reach 800 billion kWh in 2030, about 6% of national electricity use. These are regulator-reported aggregate counts and agency projections. The transcript provides no project names, capacity, commissioning, metered supply, electricity cost, renewable share, emissions or useful-compute output, and it does not identify which projects are governed by the May 2026 multi-user notice.
items.title: China's energy regulator reports 12 approved green-power direct-connection projects for computing facilities

items.content_text: A preprint re-evaluates the Neural Thickets perturb-select-vote procedure and reports that much of its measured gain does not require perturbing model weights. The authors apply a fixed random bias to output logits, select members using 200 labeled task examples, then vote across selected members. In author-reported tests on language models up to 7B parameters, this approach is statistically indistinguishable from full-weight perturbations on 22 of 28 matched model–task pairs and significantly better on three and worse on three; effects vary by task, and on USPTO the raw accuracy partly reflects a majority-class predictor. On vision tasks with train-test shift, the authors attribute gains primarily to output recalibration. The work offers an alternative explanation for the measured gains, not evidence that nearby weight-space structure is absent or that the method improves general model capability.
tags: École nationale des ponts et chaussées
items.title: Logit perturbations reproduce many reported Neural Thickets gains without changing weights

items.content_text: A distinct Oct 29 arXiv paper by Google and The University of Hong Kong authors, arXiv:2610.40578, introduces a platform-agnostic framework named VeriCUA. An earlier Oct 19 paper from a different author group uses the same acronym for a learned GUI reward verifier; the two papers are separate. The later framework gathers evidence through GUI and code checks, links findings to observed sources, and can abstain when evidence does not settle a requirement. Across five reported benchmark settings, the authors find higher agreement with reference labels than selected verifier baselines. The results are author-reported and limited to the studied environments and model setup; offline unresolved cases may fall back to an initial VLM judgment, and the paper reports substantially higher token and call costs than single-call judging.
items.title: Google and HKU report platform-agnostic verification for computer-use agents

items.content_text: A distinct Oct 19 arXiv paper, 2610.26469, introduces a learned GUI reward verifier also named VeriCUA; its authors and method differ from a later Oct 29 paper using the same acronym (arXiv:2610.40578). The earlier work trains a Judge to select checks and decide when to stop while a frozen Probe inspects live GUI state. The authors report higher agreement than prompted and passive verifiers across OSWorld, MobileWorld and WebArena-Verified, and a bounded downstream Actor-RL gain. Code and configuration details are publicly linked, but no independent reproduction was performed. The reported token comparison counts Probe use, not the full Judge, training or infrastructure cost.
tags: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
items.title: Earlier VeriCUA paper reports learned GUI verification and reward gains

items.content_text: Japan's Economic and Fiscal Policy Council held its fifteenth meeting on 29 October 2026 with AI-driven economic and social change as a formal agenda item. Advisory members submitted proposals on broader public and business AI use, labor-market transition, AI-agent responsibility, AI-related productivity and token-cost measurement, cybersecurity, domestic capability and education. A government paper described ongoing work toward a 2030 vision, cross-government reform principles and possible legal and safety-control updates, with a year-end interim summary planned. These are submitted proposals and stated work directions; the meeting record does not establish adopted law, budget allocations, implementation or measured outcomes.
items.title: Japan's economic-policy council sets out proposals on AI, work and national capability

items.content_text: ShallowDefend is a work-in-progress preprint proposing an Assess → Decide → Respond format: on each turn, a model assesses user intent, commits to a parseable safety decision, and generates a response conditioned on that decision. The authors train the decision with either a self-verified reward based on known harmful or benign dialogue labels, or an external judge reward. Across five multi-turn safety benchmarks, the paper reports average safe rates of 90.4% and 93.4% for the self-reward variant on Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen3 8B, respectively; its external-reward variant scores 92.9% and 87.6%. The paper reports that its safety lead holds under six judges. These are author-reported comparisons on two backbones, not independent replication or evidence of deployment-grade safety.
items.title: ShallowDefend trains an explicit early decision for multi-turn safety defense

items.content_text: The Ramanujan Challenge authors report an AI-assisted workflow for reviewing research-level mathematical submissions in natural language, computer algebra and Lean. It executes submitted Python under a fixed environment, has separate agents summarize the proof and code, compares those summaries, then presents the result to a human reviewer.
